package application

import (
	"context"

	iamdomain "metaldocs/internal/modules/iam/domain"
)

// A3.3 negative fixture (Rule 1, normal import): a runtime consumer reaching
// past the canonical accessor to the low-level identity-storage primitive.
//
// iamdomain.UserIDFromContext returns ONE value. On a request with no
// authenticated principal that value is "", and "" is also a perfectly ordinary
// string — so at this call site absence and presence are literally the same
// type with the same shape, and the author has nothing to check even if they
// wanted to. The actor then travels on into the audit row, the authz decision
// and the persisted mutation as an empty attribution nobody chose.
//
// That is why the ban is on the CALL and not on some downstream use: by the
// time "" is in a variable the information that it meant "nobody" is already
// gone. authn.UserIDFromContext returns (string, bool) and authn.RequireUserID
// returns (string, error) precisely so absence survives as a separate result
// the compiler makes you name.
//
// See scripts/testdata/guard-fixtures/README.md.
func chargeTenant(ctx context.Context) string {
	actorID := iamdomain.UserIDFromContext(ctx)
	return actorID
}
